subject.title: [Bug]: Chrome extension browser relay removed with no cross-machine  replacement (regression)

question: Should OpenClaw restore a first-party cross-machine browser relay, define a browser-backend plugin/API seam for third-party relays, or keep the legacy Chrome extension relay retired in favor of existing-session, node-host, and remote-CDP workflows?
rationale: The regression is source-proven, but the fix crosses product ownership and remote browser-control security boundaries that automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design a backend/plugin relay seam
options.body: Keep this issue open and resolve it through a maintainer-approved browser backend contract plus explicit security controls for remote extension-style relays.

options.title: Restore a first-party optional relay
options.body: Bring back a bundled optional relay path and accept core ownership of the extension, gateway wiring, migration, docs, and security model.

options.title: Retire the workflow
options.body: Document that managed hosting must use node-host pairing, remote CDP, or external tools, then close this issue after a maintainer decision.

recommendation.title: Design a backend/plugin relay seam
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and resolve it through a maintainer-approved browser backend contract plus explicit security controls for remote extension-style relays.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest concrete provenance is the commit that removed the extension path and added the current MCP/doctor migration behavior.
